questions.title: What are Core Web Vitals and how do you optimize them?
questions.description:
Core Web Vitals

Core Web Vitals are user-centered metrics created by Google to measure the page load speed, interactivity, and visual stability of a webpage.

The Metrics

  • Largest Contentful Paint (LCP): Measures loading performance. Targets visual rendering of the main page content within 2.5 seconds.
  • Interaction to Next Paint (INP): Measures responsiveness/interactivity. Replaced FID in March 2024. Target is <200ms.
  • Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS): Measures visual stability. Ensures unexpected layout movements do not happen. Target is <0.1.
questions.bestPractices:
• Optimize LCP by prioritizing the loading of main hero images (using fetchpriority="high").
  • Avoid layout shifts (CLS) by always reserving space for images/ads using explicit dimensions.
  • Reduce INP by splitting long tasks using requestIdleCallback or yielding threads.
questions.commonMistakes:
• Loading heavy images/videos without dimensions, causing massive layout shifts.
  • Blocking the main thread with heavy JS execution during page interactions, raising INP.
questions.example:
<!-- LCP Hero Image Optimization -->
<img 
  src="hero.webp" 
  alt="Hero" 
  width="800" 
  height="400" 
  fetchpriority="high" 
  preload="auto"
/>
questions.interviewTip: Explain INP clearly: it measures the latency of all user interactions (clicks, taps, keypresses) on a page and picks the longest response. Mention techniques like task splitting and transition management.
